# Dynamic Scene and Temporal Modeling

Also called: Dynamic NeRF, 4D Radiance Fields, Temporal NeRF

## Overview
Dynamic Scene and Temporal Modeling extends static neural radiance fields to represent and render scenes that change over time, solving the limitation of static representations for video sequences and dynamic objects [14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md]. Unlike static methods, these approaches introduce a temporal dimension to the scene representation, allowing the radiance field to vary continuously or discretely across time steps [14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md]. This family is distinguished by its diverse strategies for handling temporal dynamics: from simple input expansion of time coordinates [14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md] to complex deformation fields [15541-forward-warping-for-novel-view-synthesis.md], particle systems [15550-dynamic-appearance-particle-neural-radiance-field.md], and state-space filtering [15551-kfd-nerf.md].

## Shared principles
The core principle of this family is the expansion of the scene representation from a 3D function $f(\mathbf{x})$ to a 4D function $f(\mathbf{x}, t)$, where $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ is spatial position and $t \in \mathbb{R}$ is time [14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md]. This requires modifying the standard NeRF architecture [Parent](3065-nerf-hyperparameters.md) to accept time as an input or to deform spatial coordinates based on time.

1.  **Temporal Input Conditioning:** Time $t$ is treated as an additional input dimension, often concatenated with spatial coordinates before positional encoding [14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md].
2.  **Canonical Space and Deformation:** Many methods map dynamic points to a static "canonical" space using a deformation field $\mathbf{d}(\mathbf{x}, t)$, such that $\mathbf{x}_{can} = \mathbf{x} + \mathbf{d}(\mathbf{x}, t)$ [15541-forward-warping-for-novel-view-synthesis.md][15551-kfd-nerf.md]. The radiance field is then defined in this canonical space.
3.  **Rendering Integration:** The volume rendering integral is extended to account for time-varying density $\sigma(\mathbf{x}, t)$ and color $\mathbf{c}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d}, t)$ [15550-dynamic-appearance-particle-neural-radiance-field.md]:
    $$
    C(r, t) = \int_{s_n}^{s_f} T(s, t)\sigma(r(s), t)c(r(s), \mathbf{d}, t)ds
    $$
    where $T(s, t) = \exp\left(-\int_{s_n}^{s} \sigma(r(s'), t)ds'\right)$ [15550-dynamic-appearance-particle-neural-radiance-field.md].

## Subtopics

### [Gear-NeRF](13848-gear-nerf.md)
Stratifies the 4D scene into discrete "gear" levels based on semantic motion scales. It assigns higher-resolution feature volumes to regions with larger motion, improving efficiency and tracking quality compared to uniform sampling methods like [NeRF with Time Parameter](14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md). Choose this when scene motion is heterogeneous and object tracking is required.

### [NeRF with Time Parameter](14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md)
The baseline dynamic method that concatenates a positional-encoded time parameter to spatial coordinates in the standard two-MLP architecture. It is simple to implement but produces blurry predictions and lacks explicit dynamic reasoning. Choose this for static-like scenes with minor temporal variations or as a baseline.

### [Forward Warping for Novel View Synthesis](15541-forward-warping-for-novel-view-synthesis.md)
Models a static canonical radiance field and differentially warps it to target time steps using average splatting and an inpaint network. It solves many-to-one mapping ambiguities better than backward-flow methods. Choose this for high-fidelity novel view synthesis of dynamic scenes with significant motion.

### [Dynamic Appearance Particle Neural Radiance Field](15550-dynamic-appearance-particle-neural-radiance-field.md)
Superimposes a static grid-based field with a particle-based dynamic field, using appearance particles only for dynamic elements. It solves the problem of reconstructing time-varying scenes from monocular video without multi-view stereo data. Choose this for monocular dynamic scene reconstruction.

### [KFD-NeRF](15551-kfd-nerf.md)
Models the 4D radiance field as a dynamic system estimated using a Kalman filter, separating motion estimation into observation and prediction branches. It differs from sibling methods by explicitly handling motion dynamics via state estimation rather than direct conditioning. Choose this for scenes with smooth, predictable motion where temporal consistency is critical.

## Background
The concept of dynamic neural radiance fields emerged as a natural extension of the original NeRF [Parent](3065-nerf-hyperparameters.md) to handle video data. Early work, such as [NeRF with Time Parameter](14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md), demonstrated that simply adding time as an input could model dynamic scenes, albeit with limitations in quality [14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md]. Subsequent research introduced more sophisticated mechanisms, including deformation fields [15541-forward-warping-for-novel-view-synthesis.md], particle systems [15550-dynamic-appearance-particle-neural-radiance-field.md], and state-space filters [15551-kfd-nerf.md], to address issues like ghosting, blurriness, and computational efficiency. These methods are widely used in novel view synthesis, 4D reconstruction, and dynamic scene understanding.
